key_insight: Collective vortex escape in a pinned, spinning-down superfluid weakens boundary flow until the escape self-arrests, limiting angular momentum transfer.
engineering_relevance: The findings connect pinning thresholds, container size, and initial rotation to bounded angular momentum release in rotating superfluids.
method: Identify the minimum opening angle of a near-wall sector vacated at the onset of collective vortex escape.
Track how vortex escape reduces boundary flow and arrests further exit.
Relate depletion-region dimensions to critical unpinning velocity, container size, and initial rotation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an onset criterion and well-defined depletion-region dimensions, but provides no quantitative results or validation details.
watch_item: Relevance to pulsar glitches is discussed, but applicability beyond the studied container and pinning conditions is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Self-arresting vortex rearrangements in pinned spinning-down superfluids
